summary: Put the Position settings directly under the "In one position" button and show they belong to it
detail: The View toggle sits in its own row and the Position row appears further down, past Display and Chord, so the connection between choosing a position and the controls for moving it is not visible. Move the Position row directly beneath View and give it something - indentation, a bracket, a shared surround - that reads as "these belong to the button above".
resolution: Done 2026-09-07. The Position row moved directly under View and is marked as belonging to it: no divider of its own, indented 14px, with an accent rule down its left edge tying it to the choice that turns it on.

summary: Make "Three-chord" and "Minor three-chord" the first preset in their lists
detail: GT.progressionPresets is ordered with Blues first, so T17 opens a fresh page on a twelve-bar. Move Three-chord (major) and Minor three-chord (minor) to the top of their respective lists so those become the defaults - simpler ground to start on. The Blues entry has no mode and shows in both lists, so ordering has to account for that.
resolution: Done 2026-09-07. Three-chord and Minor three-chord moved to the head of GT.progressionPresets, major first. The picker filters by mode, so each lands at the top of its own list and T17's findIndex(fitsMode) opens a fresh page on it. Verified: major lists Three-chord, Blues, Rock vamp; minor lists Minor three-chord, Blues, Jazz cadence.

summary: Add a "randomize chords" quick action to the chord chart
detail: Beside the key picker and dice already there. It should roll: the number of chords, 2 to 4 inclusive; each chord's bar count independently, 1 or 2; then the degrees and qualities, honouring the "Common chords only" and "Use 7ths" settings the way the existing randomize does. Drive the same state as the settings panel rather than duplicating it, as the other quick actions do.
resolution: Done 2026-09-07. A second dice in the chart's quick actions rolls a whole progression: 2-4 chords, each holding 1 or 2 bars, then the degrees and shapes through the existing randomizeChords so both roll settings apply. Verified over 40 rolls - counts 2/3/4 all appear, bars only ever 1 or 2, the key is held and the preset clears; with Use 7ths on every chord came up a seventh, and turning Common chords only off widened the pool from six degrees to eight (adding III and ii deg).

summary: Add a mailto link for jeff@jeffsguitartools.com to the footer
detail: Asked for while B6 and B5 were in progress. The footer holds only the Experimental features label and the Genre examples tab.
resolution: Done 2026-09-07. A mailto: link sits beside the Genre examples button in the site footer, styled to match the footer label - muted, small caps size, with a hairline underline that brightens on hover and keyboard focus.

summary: Rename the "In one position" toggle to "All chords in one position", in Chords and Triads only
detail: The View toggle reads "Across the neck" / "In one position". The second name only describes what those two views do: Chords and Triads are the ones that bring the whole progression with you into the position, so "All chords in one position" says what you get. Pentatonic, Scales and Roots draw one thing in a position rather than every chord, so they keep the plain "In one position" - the label has to follow the Fretboard mode rather than being fixed markup. The button lives in index.html's #viewGroup and would need its text set from updateFretUI, which already runs on every mode change. Nothing reads the label as data: the view keys off data-value="position", so this is text only. The phrase also appears across README.md, the index.html tooltips, comments in js/fretboard-view.js and test names in js/tests.js and js/tests-fretboard.js - check which of those name the control (may need rewording) and which describe the reading in prose (leave).
resolution: Done 2026-09-07. The label is set from updateFretUI rather than fixed in the markup, so it follows the Fretboard mode: "All chords in one position" in Chords and Triads, plain "In one position" in Roots, Pentatonic and Scales. Text only - the reading is still chosen by data-value="position", so nothing that selects it had to change. The View tooltip and the two README passages naming the control were reworded; the prose describing the reading was left alone. Checked at 1100px and at 375px: the longer label keeps the row on one line and does not overflow. Covered by a test over all five views.

summary: When playback is paused, clicking a chord in the chart should also select that chord on the fretboard
detail: Today a click on a bar in the chord chart sounds that chord (practice.js: the bar click handler rings it). While playback is paused it should also make that chord the one the fretboard shows - the same selection the Chord row (#cagedChordGroup) makes - so tapping through the chart walks the neck through the changes. Keep the sound. While playing, Follow already moves the fretboard with the bars, so nothing changes there. Asked for on 2026-09-08 during the UI redesign; not started.
resolution: Done 2026-09-08. fretboard-view exposes selectChord(progressionIndex); practice.js calls it from the bar click handler when isPlaying is false, so the bar you tap to hear also comes onto the neck. The index has to be counted past diminished chords, which have no CAGED shapes and no button - the same counting Follow does, now factored into pickerIndexFor/showChordAt and shared by both. A diminished chord's bar and any click in Roots leave the neck alone. Covered by a new test over a progression with a dim chord in it.

summary: Quick BPM buttons below the tempo slider in the transport
detail: The Stage transport carries the tempo slider with the BPM readout beside it; the 60 / 90 / 120 shortcuts that used to sit in the floating cluster went with the redesign. Put a row of quick BPM buttons under the slider, driving #tempo the way the old .bpm-preset chips did (practice.js still binds .bpm-preset by class and marks the matching one active). Mind the phone transport, where the slider already only gets ~74px of track. Asked for on 2026-09-08; not started.
resolution: Done 2026-09-08. The tempo block in the transport is a stack: the slider and its BPM readout on top, 60 / 90 / 120 / 150 / 180 underneath (the last two added the same day). No JS was needed - practice.js already binds every .bpm-preset by class and lights whichever matches the slider. The five chips are tightened on a phone so they stay on one line and the bar stays 75px tall. The page now opens at 120.

summary: Show a style selector in the playback bar when there is room
detail: Style (Simple / Rock / Blues / Jazz / Pop / Funk, #styleGroup) lives in the Set up sheet. When the transport is wide enough - a laptop, not a phone - show the style choice in the bar itself so it can be changed without opening the sheet. It should drive the same #styleGroup state rather than keeping its own, the way the chart-head pickers drive the sheet pickers; collapse it below some width. Asked for on 2026-09-08; not started.
resolution: Done 2026-09-08. The transport names the style rather than laying it out - the chart head's move, a value in Fraunces with a caret and the real <select> lying over it invisibly, shown from 760px up. It's a view of the same state, kept in step by practice.js the way quickKey and keySelect are; the six-button row stays in the sheet as the full setting. Simple appears once per note value ('Simple quarter note' and so on), since Simple alone says nothing about what you'll hear and the note value is the only thing left to choose; picking one sets both, and changing either from the sheet renames it in the bar.

summary: A copy-link button somewhere not hidden behind Set up
detail: Copy link to this progression (#shareBtn, with #shareOut) sits under Share at the bottom of the Set up sheet. Put a share / copy-link control somewhere on the practice page itself - the chart head beside the dice and gear, or the transport - so sharing is one tap. Keep the sheet entry or drop it, but drive the same handler. Asked for on 2026-09-08; not started.
resolution: Done 2026-09-08. A link icon sits in the chart head beside the dice and the gear. practice.js's share handler was split into copyShareLink(), which writes the address bar and tries the clipboard and says whether it took; stage.js wires the icon to it, ticks for 1.8s when it worked, and falls back to opening the sheet with the selectable field when there's no clipboard. The Set up sheet keeps its own button. Both paths verified.

summary: Show the metronome click toggle in the playback footer when there is room
detail: The metronome on/off (#clickToggle, Simple style only - practice.js shows #clickRow by style) lives in the Set up sheet under Playback. When the transport is wide enough - a laptop, not a phone - show a click toggle in the bar itself so it can be flipped without opening the sheet. Drive the same #clickToggle state rather than keeping its own, the way T28 does for style; collapse it below some width, and hide it whenever the sheet row is hidden. Asked for on 2026-09-08; not started.
resolution: Done 2026-09-08. stage.js moves the sheet's own click row into a slot in the transport above 900px and back below it - and back into the sheet whenever the sheet is open, so a settings sheet is never missing a setting. One row, two homes, nothing to keep in step. It stays hidden when the style isn't Simple, wherever it is: practice.js sets clickRow.hidden and that follows the element. Renamed from 'Metronome' to 'Click' the same day.

summary: Remove the "position: frets 1–4" entry from the fretboard legend
detail: fretboard-view.js appends "position: frets lo–hi" to #cagedLegend in the position reading (three places, around lines 1286, 1306 and 1358). The Stage layout draws the position on the neck itself as a labelled window, so the legend entry now says the same thing twice. Mind that stage.js placeWindow() currently reads that legend text to place the window - it needs another source for lo/hi first (expose the shown window from fretboard-view, or a data attribute on the legend), and any test that looks for the legend text (js/tests-fretboard.js) must be updated. Asked for on 2026-09-08; not started.
resolution: Done 2026-09-08. renderFretLegend publishes the position as data-window="3-7" on #cagedLegend instead of pushing a "position: frets 3-7" entry into the legend, so the neck's own labelled window is the only place it's said. stage.js reads the attribute (and observes it), and the three tests that read the words now read the attribute. New test asserts the attribute is there in the position reading of all four box views and that no legend entry spells it out.

summary: The chord finder gives too little to go on when the input is empty
detail: With no chord typed, the page is a bare input, a "Chord" label and a line of hint text - nothing shows what the tool does or what a result looks like, and on a phone the hint is easy to miss. Give the empty state something to act on: a heading or sentence saying what the tool is for, the example chord names as buttons that fill the input rather than prose ("Try things like C, Am7, F#dim..."), and/or autofocus the field. Consider showing a worked example (one chord already searched) instead of an empty page. Asked for on 2026-09-08 after the Stage rebuild; not started.
resolution: Done 2026-09-08. The prose list of example chord names became a row of buttons that fill the field, and the field takes focus when you arrive on the tab with nothing typed. The 'Dots show' row waits until there's a chord to label. Jeff then had both explanatory paragraphs removed, so the empty page is the field, the examples and nothing else.

summary: Split "Play notes" into "Play chord" and "Play arpeggio"
detail: reverse-finder.js binds #reversePlayBtn to GT.chordFinder.strum(cells), which sweeps the picked notes low to high like a pick across the strings - one gesture, no way to hear the notes ring together or to hear them one at a time slowly. Replace the single button with two: a chord (all notes at once, or a fast strum as now) and an arpeggio (the notes spaced out, low to high, slow enough to hear each). chord-finder.js owns strum(); it likely needs a companion or a spacing argument rather than a second copy of the note-firing code. Asked for on 2026-09-08 after the Stage rebuild; not started.
resolution: Done 2026-09-08. strum() takes the gap between notes as an argument - the one thing that separates a strum from an arpeggio - and holds each note longer as the gap grows, so a slow roll still adds up to the chord. Play chord keeps the old 18ms sweep; Play arpeggio uses 280ms. No second copy of the note-firing code.

summary: Add a play/pause button to the left of the key display at the top
detail: The Stage layout has one Play, pinned in the transport at the bottom. Add a second one at the head of the chart, left of the key title, so playback can be started without looking away from the chart (the old layout had one in the chart panel corner for the same reason). It should be the same control, not a second state: practice.js binds every .play-btn and sets the icon and aria-label on all of them together, so a button with that class in the chart head is wired for free - it just needs sizing that suits the chart head (smaller than the 54px transport circle) and a check that the head still wraps sanely on a phone. Asked for on 2026-09-08; not started.
resolution: Done 2026-09-08. A 38px Play sits at the head of the chart row, left of the key. It carries the .play-btn class, which practice.js already binds as a set - it sets the icon and aria-label on all of them together - so it's the same control at a second size, not a second state.
